IT’S TIME TO TAKE ON THE GREED OF THE FOSSIL FUEL INDUSTRY The vast majority of scientists tell us that the climate crisis is fueling heat waves and extreme weather across the globe. Donald Trump tells us that climate change is a “hoax.” Who is right? Let’s look at the facts. The last eleven years have been the hottest eleven years on record. The last three years have been the hottest three years on record. 2026 will be one of the warmest years on record, and most scientists believe 2027 will be the warmest year in recorded history. This summer alone, Europe has seen three record heat waves – including the continent’s worst on record that killed more than 10,000 people – and is about to experience its FOURTH of the year. The United States, which has already seen two record heat waves that exposed hundreds of millions of people to dangerous temperatures, is currently experiencing its third major heat wave of the year. This heat is exacerbating drought conditions across the world, including the worst spring drought on record in the United States and some of Europe’s driest conditions on record this summer. We are seeing massive wildfires across the northern hemisphere, including hundreds of wildfires in the United States and Canada earlier this month that created dangerous air quality for Americans across the country. Huge fires that are burning right now in Oregon, Washington and western Canada will create even more dangerous air across the United States over the coming week. In Europe, France and Spain are seeing unprecedented wildfires that have forced more than 300,000 people to evacuate their homes. Major fires are also burning in Portugal, Greece, Italy and Turkey. We are seeing new and extraordinarily dangerous flash flooding become normal across the United States. Alaska, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania and West Virginia have all seen record rainfalls this summer that have driven dangerous flash flooding events. Texas Hill Country just saw a 1,000-year rainfall event, its second in two years, that dumped almost a year’s worth of rainfall in just a few days. Missouri just saw a 1,000-year rainfall event that forced emergency responders to rescue campers from cabin rooftops and trees. And it’s not just the United States dealing with extreme flooding – massive floods displaced thousands earlier this summer in West Africa. Recent rainfall in Pakistan killed more than 100 people. And just last week, enormous flooding in India displaced more than 700,000 people. In the face of this extraordinary and devastating reality, Donald Trump continues to protect his fossil fuel billionaire friends that are driving this global crisis. Our job is to take on his ignorance and the greed of the fossil fuel industry by transforming our energy system away from fossil fuels to energy efficiency and sustainable sources of power. If we are to provide a healthy and habitable planet for future generations, this is a struggle that must be won.

GAZA: THE SUFFERING CONTINUES Today in Gaza, most of the TV cameras are gone and media interest has declined. But, more than nine months after the announcement of a supposed “ceasefire”, the suffering of the Palestinian people continues. Today, 92% of housing units in Gaza are damaged or destroyed, 70% of the entire population lacks adequate housing and is forced to live in makeshift shelters, 86% of agricultural water wells have been damaged, the vast majority of households report significant challenges in accessing safe and clean sanitation facilities and 90% of all energy infrastructure has been destroyed. And what about the children? Today in Gaza, 91% of school-aged children do not have sustained access to in-person education, 93% of school buildings will require full reconstruction or major rehabilitation to be functional again and 70% of infants and young children under two years of age are experiencing moderate to severe food insecurity. All of this is taking place after the horrific destruction that Netanyahu’s extremist government brought to Gaza over the last three years: more than 73,000 Palestinians killed and 173,000 wounded — mostly women, children and the elderly. In addition, virtually the entire infrastructure of Gaza was destroyed. Israel now controls an estimated 70% of Gaza, well beyond what they agreed to, and has built dozens of military outposts inside Gaza since the “ceasefire” began. In the nine months since the “ceasefire” was announced, Israel has killed at least 1,150 Palestinians, including a family of six last week. Now, as if to remove any doubt about their intentions, senior leaders of the Netanyahu government are moving to make the occupation permanent. Recently, a number of government ministers led thousands of settlers to the Gaza border demanding new illegal Jewish settlements be built there. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir stood up and said "Gaza is ours." The shameful fact is that the United States is complicit in everything that is happening in Gaza. We have funneled tens of billions of dollars in military aid to an Israeli government that has consistently violated international law and whose leader is a war criminal. The good news is that the American people are catching on. More and more Americans — Democrats, Republicans and independents — are demanding that we stop all military aid to Israel and use our considerable leverage to end the suffering of the Palestinian people. Enough is enough! Congress must listen to the American people. NO MORE U.S. MILITARY AID TO ISRAEL.

Today, the landmark INSULIN Act that I authored with @SenatorShaheen, @SenatorWarnock, and @SenJohnKennedy advanced out of the Senate HELP Committee by a strong bipartisan vote of 17–5, marking a critical step toward getting this legislation signed into law. B001257.text: I was proud to co-sponsor the TAKE IT DOWN Act, which is now the law of the land. No one should have to endure the trauma of having an intimate image shared online without their consent. This landmark law gives victims an important new tool by requiring covered online platforms to provide a process for requesting the removal of nonconsensual intimate images. Once a valid request is submitted, platforms must remove the image and any known identical copies within 48 hours. If a platform fails to provide a takedown process or does not comply with the law, you can report it to the Federal Trade Commission at http://TakeItDown.ftc.gov. Every report helps hold online platforms accountable and protects others from becoming victims. Watch this short video to learn more: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K53PnqfnFFY

B000490.text: This week, the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, appeared before the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government. During the hearing, I asked the Director about how Congress can be any clearer to ensure that the Trump Administration understands that once a funding bill is signed into law, the President is not allowed to change or second-guess the spending and withhold it due to policy or political differences. That is at the heart of Article 1 of the U.S. Constitution and why Congress also passed the Impoundment Control Act of 1974, when President Nixon tried to withhold funds that were already obligated according to the law.

This week, I asked the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, to explain how poorly planned cuts to the federal workforce last year have weakened services and protections upon which Americans rely. This includes the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, which is responsible for protecting America’s agriculture from invasive species and diseases. USDA-APHIS began mounting a vigorous response to the resurgence of New World Screwworm – a deadly parasite affecting livestock – in 2024. However, in early 2025, the Administration illegally fired workers and forced others to resign, causing over 25 percent of all USDA-APHIS employees to leave. USDA’s New World Screwworm prevention, monitoring, surveillance, and control efforts were halted. USDA had approved $378 million in prevention and control funding for sterile fly facilities in 2023 and 2024, yet the money went unspent when the new administration paused funding. This is extremely concerning to our ranchers, and this outbreak could drive the price of food even higher. Unfortunately, we continue to see the fallout of the blunt and ill-considered cuts to federal workers, from the return of New World Screwworm to the United States, to farmers showing up to closed or understaffed Farm Service Agency offices, to attacks on our nuclear safety programs putting national security at risk. I will continue to hold the White House accountable, as I did this week during the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government hearing with Mr. Vought.

R to @RepYvetteClarke: This dark day never would have arrived under a moral administration, and yet it could only have ever been an inevitability under Donald Trump’s. Already, his hired goons within ICE and DHS are mobilizing to terrorize our neighbors and tear apart their families. They hope to spread fear far and wide throughout our communities, until their distorted vision for America is all there is to see. In the face of such un-American injustice, we will not yield.

I, and my like-minded colleagues on both sides of the aisle, will continue to fight for your families. We will continue to advocate for our legislation to restore your rightful status and ensure you stay precisely where you belong – in the communities you have only made better across your years as our neighbors. And we will continue the work of building a nation that deserves you, and earns your forgiveness. This president may have broken the promise of America, but we will not rest until it is made whole again.

For 250 years, our great experiment has faltered, flourished, evolved, and progressed. The American experience is ever-changing and as diverse as the people who call this country home. But one thing has remained constant – the idea of America has always been a beacon of hope. Protecting this country and the ideals and values it was founded on takes work. Democracy is demanding. It takes dedication and principle. And it takes the resounding belief that upholding those ideals and values is worth the fight because America is bigger than any one person. Because liberty can only truly endure when it is paired with responsibility, virtue, and a commitment to put public good ahead of personal ambition. Today, we celebrate the moment when our founding fathers openly declared that creating this country, based in liberty, was a necessity in the face of tyranny. Their legacy is that leadership requires courage when it’s difficult, integrity when no one is watching, and a willingness to put country above self. We must remember that our duty is not merely to the next election, but to the next generation. That should be the challenge for all Americans as we look forward to another 250 years. From Massachusetts, where the fight for freedom first began, I wish you a happy 4th of July. God Bless America always, God Bless all who call her home, and God Bless our courageous men and women in uniform who continue the fight for liberty today.

On Monday, our office suffered an unimaginable loss. Chris Matthews, my District Outreach and Communications Director, passed away unexpectedly. If any one of you begin to lose faith in our country, remember Chris Matthews. Remember he was without question one of the Commonwealth’s sharpest political minds – a generational talent. Remember that he was more than a Congressional aide. He took the belief that through our actions we all can bring needed change and brought it with him on many interstate bus rides to canvas distant pivotal states and to the doors of the families he inspired. Remember through his example that public service is a genuinely noble vocation. As a trusted member of our office, he helped countless veterans, families, and those who could not advocate for themselves. Those of us privileged to have worked with him for over fifteen years will remember his laugh and his wry, often biting, humor – contrasting the way things are to the way they could be. We will always remember his authentic belief that in this country, people can bring about progress and meaningful change. It was real to him and his sincerity shown through. Chris was a genuinely good person. He was family to all of us, and we are devastated by his loss, particularly at such a young age. Our thoughts and prayers are with Molly and Eli and the many who loved him. Though we wish we had more time with him, his memory will continue to give us faith that one person can significantly make better the lives of those around him.

As Chairman of the House Veterans' Affairs Committee, I introduced the Take Care of America's Veterans Act, the largest expansion of veterans' health care and benefits in a decade. We’re ending the wounded veteran tax on combat-injured heroes, empowering rural veterans to get care faster and closer to home, protecting benefits for surviving spouses, and increasing support for our most severely injured veterans. Congress needs to pass this historic legislation and deliver for the men and women who served. Our veterans kept their promise to us, now it’s our turn.

Peace through strength isn’t just a slogan. It means having the factories, shipyards, and supply chains to build what our military needs, and never depending on our adversaries for it. Today I voted for the National Defense Authorization Act to bring defense production back home, strengthen our deterrence against China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea, and give our service members a well-earned pay raise along with better housing and childcare for the families who serve right alongside them. I first met Luke Tynan in 2018, not long after a diving accident at just 19 years old left him paralyzed from the waist down. In an instant, his life changed. What never changed was Luke: his determination, his faith in what is possible, and the extraordinary spirit that has inspired an entire community to stand beside him. In the years since, Luke has worked relentlessly toward his goal of walking again. But his story is about far more than recovery. It is about meeting unimaginable adversity with courage, choosing hope again and again, and somehow continuing to lift others up along the way. Now in its ninth year, the #LukeStrong Tournament has grown into one of Middletown’s most special traditions—a celebration of the young man at its heart and of the community that has never stopped standing beside him. To Luke and the entire #LukeStrong community: thank you for year after year demonstrating the power of unity, positivity, and support.

Financial fraud has become a booming criminal business, and Americans are the primary target. Nearly 15 million people were scammed last year, totaling an estimated $196 billion. Senior losses have quadrupled since 2020, with the average senior victim losing $83,000. Tragically, 1 in 4 victims of serious scams contemplate suicide. These alarming statistics got @FinancialCmte Chairman @RepFrenchHill and myself involved. We convened roundtables with banks, telecom companies, social media platforms, DOJ, FBI, FTC, FCC, the Fed, and state AGs — bringing everyone who touches this problem to the same table. I also launched http://meuser.house.gov/scams so constituents have one place to recognize and report a scam before it costs them everything. That yearlong investigation has culminated in our subcommittee’s staff report, entitled “Fighting Back.” It exposes how scamming has become an organized, for-profit industry, much of it run by Chinese-linked criminal networks operating scam compounds across Southeast Asia. The report concludes with solutions to fight back, including my legislation, the SCAM Act, and other bills that hold bad actors accountable and coordinate agencies to stop scams before they start. D000230.text: Behind every statistic is a family, a neighbor, or a small business owner who worked hard for what they have. During the past year, internet crimes cost Americans nearly $21 billion. These crimes threaten not only financial security but also peace of mind. Our office is working to strengthen consumer protections, prevent fraud, and support efforts to hold scammers accountable. The legislation below addresses several aspects of combating scams and protecting consumers. ▪️ H.R. 9668, the Safeguarding Transactions to Outpace Predatory (STOP) Senior Fraud Act, which I introduced with Rep. Zach Nunn (IA-03). The bill would help financial institutions protect older adults and other vulnerable individuals from financial exploitation by authorizing them to refuse or temporarily delay certain transactions when they reasonably believe exploitation has occurred, is occurring, or is being attempted. ▪️ H.R. 7548, the Safeguarding Consumers from Advertising Misconduct (SCAM) Act, would require online platforms to take reasonable steps to prevent fraudulent and deceptive advertisements, strengthen accountability when scams occur, and enhance enforcement of consumer protection laws by the Federal Trade Commission and state authorities. ▪️ H.R. 5490, the Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act, would establish an interagency federal task force to disrupt overseas scam operations, impose sanctions on the individuals and entities that run them, press governments that enable them, and better protect American consumers from devastating financial losses.

M001228.text: RT by @RepMaloyUtah: On Pioneer Day, I had the opportunity to tour Beaver and see firsthand the devastating impact of both wildfire and flooding. Standing in those burned and flooded landscapes, talking with the Forest Service personnel, local leaders, and the people of Beaver one thing was crystal clear: forest management works. The difference between treated and untreated forest was visible. Areas that had been thinned or otherwise managed gave firefighters a chance. They slowed the fire, reduced its intensity, helped crews establish containment lines, and in some cases, stopped the fire altogether. In the overgrown, untreated areas, the fire burned hotter, moved faster, and left behind far greater destruction, burning an unprecedented 70,000 acres in two days. It's frustrating that while the United States is the world's largest importer of lumber and paper products, millions of acres of our own forests sit overcrowded and vulnerable to catastrophic wildfire. The boots-on-the-ground Forest Service personnel managing these forests know what needs to be done and want to actively manage these lands, but too often commonsense projects are delayed or stopped by endless litigation and opposition by environmentalists and bureaucrats in Washington D.C. That's why the Fix Our Forests Act deserves to move forward. The legislation passed the House with strong bipartisan support, but has been stalled in the Senate for 18 months. It needs to move forward. I'm grateful to Congresswoman Celeste Maloy for bringing us together to see this firsthand, and to the Trump Administration officials who came to Utah to witness these conditions on the ground. With the U.S. Forest Service headquarters coming to Utah, we have a tremendous opportunity to ensure the people making decisions about our forests are closer to the landscapes and communities they serve. Thank you to USDA's Michael Boren, Sam Crofts from the Bureau of Land Management, and Chairman Bruce Westerman of the House Natural Resources Committee for taking the time to be there and hear directly from those who have been impacted by this catastrophe. On Pioneer Day weekend, that lesson feels especially meaningful. S001201.text: ROAD TO 250: Long Island & Queens Legacies Target Rock in Lloyd Harbor is more than a scenic landmark—it is a reminder of Long Island’s place in our nation’s history. The wildlife refuge takes its name from a 14-foot-tall glacial boulder standing just offshore in Huntington Bay. For generations, the rock served as a navigation marker for mariners and was reportedly used for cannon and target practice during both the Revolutionary War and the War of 1812. During the American Revolution, the British established "East Fort" nearby to help defend the harbor, and Lloyd Neck became home to Loyalists displaced by the conflict. As America approaches its 250th anniversary, places like Target Rock help tell the story of how the Revolutionary War shaped communities here on Long Island and across the nation.

B001323.text: This landmark investment by the U.S. Space Force is a tremendous win for Alaska and America’s national security! The Pacific Spaceport Complex-Alaska in Kodiak is uniquely positioned to support rapid, responsive launch capabilities. I’ve had the opportunity to personally tour our Kodiak spaceport and see firsthand the incredible potential of this facility. It's clear that Alaska offers a strategic advantage few places in the world can match, with the infrastructure and geography to support the next generation of defense and space innovation. We discussed the tremendous potential of the Kodiak Spaceport Complex, one of the nation's critical commercial launch sites, as well as Poker Flat Research Range outside of Fairbanks, the world's only university-owned rocket range and a cornerstone of atmospheric and space research.   As investment in aerospace continues to grow, we have an incredible opportunity to prepare Alaska's students, engineers and technicians for high-paying careers right here at home. By strengthening partnerships with NASA, our universities, our military installations, and the private sector, we can ensure Alaska remains a key player in space innovation.   I appreciate Administrator Isaacman taking the time to discuss our shared vision and look forward to working together to ensure Alaska continues to serve as a vital launch point for discovery and as a key component in our nation's space leadership strategy.

Was für eine abscheuliche Tat in Berlin. Hunderttausende Menschen aus aller Welt feierten friedlich beim Christopher Street Day. Sie wollten, dass wir gut und tolerant miteinander umgehen. Das ist ein Angriff auf unsere Gesellschaft.

R to @bundeskanzler: Wir sind offen und freiheitsliebend - und das werden wir auch bewahren und verteidigen. Die Tat wird aufgeklärt und mit aller Härte verfolgt. Meine Gedanken sind bei den Betroffenen und ihren Angehörigen. Ich wünsche den Verletzten rasche Genesung und danke allen Einsatzkräften.

WORLD_INDIA_PM.text: Greetings to all wildlife enthusiasts on Global Tiger Day. The people of India are proud of the fact that we are home to almost 70% of the global tiger population. India’s tiger conservation efforts are inspired by our centuries-old culture of living in harmony with nature and powered by the collective will of our people. We also reaffirm our commitment to science-based conservation, community participation and sustainable development that strengthens tiger conservation.

R to @narendramodi: The efforts and dedication of our forest personnel, scientists and conservationists have also played a key role in tiger protection. In that spirit, India remains committed to empowering local communities and reducing human-wildlife conflict.
